newsitem.title: USA: Miami Int'l cargo off two percent in February.
newsitem.headline: Miami Int'l cargo off two percent in February.

text.p: Despite a dip in cargo volumes in February, officials at Miami International Airport said Monday they expected healthy growth would resume.
"There is no reason for us to think that we will not see strong continued growth," Naomi Nixon, the airport's manager of marketing and trade development, said.
"We are expecting a very strong April and May," Peter Reaveley, MIA head of route development, said.
All cargo, including mail, amounted to 151,101 tons in February, a 2.12 percent decline from February 1996, according to statistics compiled by Dade County Aviation Department.
International cargo, including mail, totaled 123,574 tons, up 1.17 percent from the same month of 1996. Domestic cargo, including mail, amounted to 27,527, down 14.59 percent.

Year to date, all cargo amounted to 292,175 tons, about even with the first two months of 1996. For the latest 12 months, cargo totaled 1.88 million tons, according to Dade County Aviation statistics.
